note.title: Nonsmooth proximal foundation: compare the convex loss at an actual minimizer
note.plain: A convex loss need not be differentiable to obtain this comparison. Supply an actual minimum of loss plus a differentiable perturbation, then compare the loss with every feasible competitor. E is a real normed vector space; V is a subset, p belongs toV, and f:E->R is convex onV (including convexity ofV). The supplied p actually minimizes f+h overV. Only h has a specified ambient continuous Frechet derivative atp. No derivative or continuity of f, convexity of h, completeness/inner product/finite dimension, or closed/open/bounded/coercive V is assumed. EmptyV is ruled out by p membership; boundary/singleton/lower-dimensional sets and u=p are allowed. Every comparator u belongs to the sameV.
note.intuition: Move a small positive distance toward a feasible comparator. Convexity controls the loss by its endpoint values; only the perturbation is differentiated.
note.why: Lower the required general prescient proof frontier without imposing smoothness on the loss.

Derived loss-comparison dependency, not the complete source theorem. Theorem2.8 printed11/PDF23 explicitly assumes a differentiable objective and is not applied to a nonsmooth f+h here. note.proof_idea: Fix u inV and put q(a)=p+a(u-p),0<=a<=1. Feasibility follows from convexity ofV. Actual minimality and convexity of f give f(p)+h(p)<=f(q(a))+h(q(a))<=(1-a)f(p)+a f(u)+h(q(a)). Hence H(a)=a(f(u)-f(p))+h(q(a))-h(p)>=0=H(0). Differentiate only h along the affine segment: Hprime(0)=f(u)-f(p)+Dh(p)[u-p]. At a minimum on[0,1], the positive tangent direction1 gives Hprime(0)>=0. Rearranging yields f(p)-f(u)<=Dh(p)[u-p]. This proves the loss comparison from an actual minimum, without a supplied regret/stability bound or differentiability of the loss.

Actual pinned Mathlib facts: IsLocalMinOn.hasFDerivWithinAt_nonneg, sub_mem_posTangentConeAt_of_segment_subset, Convex.segment_subset, HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq, scalar derivative composition/addition, and continuous-linear evaluation. No previous ABRL theorem is a direct VALUE parent of this proof; the source mapping and planned Bregman consumer are overlays, not formal implication edges. Three actual Test families prove their minimizing conditions and derivative data: f(z)=abs(z),h(z)=(z-1/2)^2/2,p=0 with a genuinely nonsmooth loss; f(z)=z,h(z)=-z/2 on[0,1],p=0, which is not a whole-line minimum; and f(z)=z^2,h(z)=-z^2/2+z,p=-1 with a nonconvex regularizer. Their universal comparisons use the same public helper. Two numerical endpoints retain the helper in their separately selected compiled final conjuncts via expression-equality transport. These Tests are not additional source results or an existence algorithm. One reusable real-valued convex minimizer comparison, explicitly generalized to arbitrary real normed spaces.
